gaps.construct: NUL-terminated char* walked with a++ / b++ and read past the shorter string up to its terminator
gaps.description: No pointers or terminated strings; modelled as Bytes plus a byte_at helper that returns 0 at or past the end. Behaviour matches for well-formed C strings, but the type no longer says the input is unbounded and borrowed.

gaps.construct: null pointer checks zLeft==0 and zRight==0
gaps.description: Expressible as maybe Bytes with two nested chooses; the four-way null handling takes 10 lines instead of 4, and the `when some right` arm must bind a name it never uses.

gaps.construct: post-decrement inside the loop condition, N-- > 0, and the later N<0 test
gaps.description: No assignment inside expressions (by design), so the side effect in the condition was unrolled; the C trick of using N<0 to mean 'ran out of budget' had to be re-derived as remaining <= 0, which is a behaviour-preserving but non-obvious rewrite.
The doc does not say whether a module-level constant (`let` outside an operation) is allowed or how a table literal of 256 bytes is written; replaced by a pure operation header.

gaps.construct: (unsigned char *) cast and byte arithmetic producing a signed int difference
gaps.description: No byte type or casts are documented; Byte was declared as a refined Int, and the subtraction is assumed to give an Int.

gaps.construct: calling an operation on a parenthesised argument: upper_to_lower (byte_at i of left)
gaps.description: The doc shows parentheses only for arithmetic grouping and `item (i + 1) of items`; nesting one call inside another call's argument is not shown.

notes: The `no assignment inside expressions` rule did exactly what it promises here: the C condition hides a decrement whose off-by-one effect on the final N<0 test is easy to misread, and the Scribe version makes it explicit. Pointer-walking string code needs a documented answer for terminated strings and borrowed byte views.
